mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in post-rate-hike periods are not statistically different from pre-hike periods (t-test p > 0.05), or discount rate sensitivity (Rank IC) is below 0.05 over the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the CPIAUCSL inflation index below 2% for three consecutive months reduce the Fed’s incentive to tighten policy, lowering real risk-free rates and thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of no-inflation movement (p > 0.10), or the IC for CPIAUCSL vs. 10Y Treasury yield is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 jobs in a month coincides with rising consumer confidence (HOUST), jointly signaling a strong labor market and optimism that supports higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 50,000 and HOUST rises in the same month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows meeting the trigger, forward returns are negative on average, or the interaction IC (joint significance) is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 3% in a month indicates weakening supply-side momentum, reducing expected future earnings and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 3% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in subsequent months are not statistically worse than a neutral baseline (p > 0.10), or the IC for INDPRO is below 0.10 over the 5-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but proxy via RSAFS: retail advances) exceeding 10% in two months signals accelerating consumer demand, which elevates equity risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by more than 10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows meeting the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10), or the IC for RSAFS vs. S&P 500 returns is below 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for four consecutive months, accompanied by a sustained drop in job openings (implied by low RSAFS), suggests a tight labor market that raises inflationary expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for four consecutive months and RSAFS remains low
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such regimes are not statistically negative (p > 0.10), or the interaction IC between UNRATE and RSAFS is below 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS behavior) below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a flattening yield curve, which reduces real borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses below 3.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in subsequent months are not statistically higher than during a neutral yield curve slope (p > 0.10), or the IC for FEDFUNDS vs. S&P 500 returns is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed within the same month by a decline in consumer confidence (HOUST) below 1100 suggests dual softening in supply and sentiment, which depresses growth forecasts and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls and HOUST falls in the same month
regime_hint: Dual soft landing risk turning into soft landing scare
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after such a dual fall, forward returns are not statistically worse than a neutral baseline (p > 0.10), or the interaction IC between INDPRO and HOUST is below 0.10.
